title: Define opaque-response blocking (updated)
body: Define opaque-response blocking Opaque-response blocking (ORB) blocks cross-origin no-cors responses that are unlikely to be CSS, JavaScript, images, or media, so they don't reach the process that requested them, where side channels could reveal their contents. Responses to fetch() that would be blocked get a null body instead. Media requests use a new no-cors media request state, and audio and video are sniffed using the MIME Sniffing Standard. This supersedes #1442. Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64714. Fixes #721. *** Based on #1442 by @annevk, with "validate a partial response", the `Content-Range` parser, and Gecko's changes added by @sefeng211. @farre and @zcorpan have since aligned it with Gecko and Chromium; see the status comments for what changed and why. Related: - whatwg/html#12914 sets the no-cors media request state and fallback encoding for media elements and classic scripts. - whatwg/mimesniff#219 adds the audio and video signatures ORB relies on; whatwg/mimesniff#218 is about how many bytes ADTS needs. - whatwg/fetch#1966 and w3c-fedid/FedCM#852 replace the FedCM exemption with "user-agent-no-cors". Needs input from Chromium or WebKit: - [ ] annevk/orb#30 (both): sniffing JavaScript-labeled responses for JSON or parser breakers. - [ ] Q1 in https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/1755#issuecomment-6684663759 (both): case-insensitive `bytes` in `Content-Range`. - [ ] whatwg/mimesniff#218 (both): bytes needed to sniff ADTS. - [ ] whatwg/mimesniff#219 (both): audio and video signatures. - [ ] annevk/orb#43, annevk/orb#38, annevk/orb#22 (Chromium): whether to implement the full JavaScript-and-not-JSON check. - [ ] annevk/orb#3 (both): future image types. - [ ] annevk/orb#32 (Chromium): signed exchanges. - [ ] https://issues.chromium.org/issues/581932194 (Chromium): step 8. To do: - [x] Address the rest of @annevk's [AI review](https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/pull/1755#issuecomment-6627472873). - [ ] Land WICG/background-fetch#181 (uses Fetch's exported "extract content-range values" and "validate a partial response") after this. - [ ] Apply the outcomes of the "Needs input" items above. - [x] annevk/orb#7: decode with the same encoding for the JSON check as for the JavaScript check. - [x] annevk/orb#29: HLS is mostly handled (labels, `#EXTM3U` and MPEG-TS sniffing, step 8); "subsequent" is now tied to URLs that sniffed as audio or video. - [ ] Remove the FedCM exemption once whatwg/fetch#1966 lands. - [ ] PR to make tests non-tentative. *** - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Chromium * Gecko - [ ] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64714 * https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/orb/tentative?label=experimental&label=master&aligned * Non-tentative: to do - [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/581932194 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2089487, https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2089454 * WebKit: … - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
